The wheel broke before dusk. We left the iron fittings under the bound box and carried the grain away. A repair order is tucked between the pages: "Take the bent blades to Godot’s woodland forge. He works with a young crossbow maker. Keep to the old cart tracks through the woods." The margins record bends and stream crossings.

dynamic_line: The open clearing is watched. I saw the trees move while the air was still. I tied the pack above the washout and took the lower path to see whether the other bank was clear. If I fail to return, keep to stone and leave room to turn back.

We leave before the next dusk. The water is clean; whoever follows may need the blanket more than we do. The smith Godot repaired our broken blade at his woodland forge. His young helper makes crossbow bolts. We copied the way back here: the old track, the stream crossing, then the charcoal burners’ path. It is a long walk, but there is a master at its end.

responses.text: Look up the woodland forge in my journal.

dynamic_line: Flora's notes: boil clean cloth for dressings; sew a waterskin before a long journey. A defensible room, drinking water, a bed and a small stone-and-bone ward make a refuge. The ward quiets new Brand summons within eight tiles, not existing enemies. Neither the missing hand nor eye will grow back through rest.

The pages survived because someone chose to carry them. Flora compares the joined worlds to roots grafted across a wound. A quiet place can shelter a traveler; no single refuge can mend the whole world. These notes grant no combat power.
A leaf-shaped wooden bookmark survived inside the stone-lined root niche. Its little inscription reads: leave a light for the next traveler.
Between the burned edges are a broken road, a ruined foundation and marks around a split in the ground. The hollow’s keeper carried this route to another breach.

responses.text: View the trail to the Ashen Breach.

dynamic_line: Fresh cuts stop halfway through the roots. Two sets of tally marks were scratched into the haft; one ends abruptly. They meant to cut a path to the stone face, not to fight what lived beneath it.
The inscription names two travelers and asks that both return home. A second knot was added with a shaking hand. Beyond it, the bark bears the same dark stain as the abandoned cutting tool.

We left the cart on the old track. The face is caught in the roots, just as he said. At the eastern edge, the bones rang and the thing beneath the trunk turned toward them. I waited behind the thick roots until it passed. We will return by the old western track. If only one of us reaches the cart, leave the other name on the cord.

Dry the herbs separately. Boil clean cloth for wounds. Mend the old sleeves before another journey. Keep both paths around the spiritual tree clear. The last line reads: a refuge remains a refuge because someone cares for it.

I marked the wide gallery to the east. Below it, the smaller passage winds around the stone mass and meets the gallery twice. We heard the chime in the western chamber before we saw what followed it. The turns hid us from its eyes. There is a braced chute near the ladder, but its peg faces deeper into the cave. I will leave another mark by the broken prop if we reach it.

Water was stored in the east room; blankets and dressings in the sacristy. An earlier entry records a traveler who brought a repaired sword and bolts: "Godot’s forge is still working in the woods. The old man and his young helper take useful metal for their work." He drew the road on the back of the page. Later entries stop counting meals and count hours beside the red stone. The last volunteer wrote: "This was meant to be a shelter."

responses.text: Look up the woodland forge in my journal.

dynamic_line: We called the stone a miracle because we needed one. We moved it behind the altar and stopped opening the door to strangers. When the whispers began, we thought we had been answered. The handprints on the altar were not made in prayer.

If the chapel is lost, leave through the broken west wall. An old cart track farther into the forest ends at a huge oak with knotted roots. Travelers spoke of another stone face there. This is a lead, not a surveyed map; do not mistake the tree for safety.

The transport order is crossed out. Below it: Three of us described the same red face after sleeping here. When we moved the specimen, the scratching began outside its new tent. Pavel is hurt; the creature caught him when he stepped into the open. Cancel collection of the sample. Send transport for the wounded. We are leaving the equipment.
We broke the shields to make a wall. Held the gap until the wounded had passed. There is no road back. Keep the pale trail in sight. The great ribs bend toward the gathering.

Names repeat on the execution notices. Shoes and cloaks were sorted before the sentence, as though the owner had already ceased to be a person. One entry was crossed out and replaced by 'sent below'. There is no altar here: terror was an ordinary office routine.

The early pages discuss boiled linen and ordinary wounds. Later sketches show an extra mouth growing through a servant's chest. The writer stopped calling it an illness: fragments of the master's flesh were forcing a second life into the victim. His treatment could not reverse it. The servants are finite, not a renewing garrison.

The ribbon lay beside sewing and a book kept clear of dust. A note calls the room Theresia's and orders the servants not to disturb it. The same ruler who signed the prison lists protected this little island of ordinary life. Her whereabouts are not recorded; the servants kept this door closed as the rest of the house fell apart.

Two roads are marked on the map. One bears the Black Dogs’ camp and Wyald’s name; the other, a mist-filled valley and Rosine’s name. Notes along the edges describe missing wagons and roads that have been closed.

The lists separate soldiers, prisoners and those taken to the leader. Human boot sizes and ration counts fill the early pages. Later marks describe warped guards wearing the same uniforms. This was an army before its cruelty took a monstrous shape. The broken wagon lies west of the tents; the quarry leaves a southern way around the cages.

I hid this before they counted us. The cage doors are tied, not locked with iron keys. Untie them from either side and pass through; the quarry is longer but stays open. One name at the bottom is followed by a small word: escaped.

Wyald ordered the stolen stores counted and the fighting ground cleared. Timber screens were dragged to its edges; three wrecked barriers remain on the open earth. Leave space beside them for a sidestep when he braces to charge. The last order names a world broken open: his old fate was diverted by the crossing, and the being leading this camp is alive, not an echo.

They called the winged things fairies because the flowers were beautiful. I followed their lost shoes past the games to the silk. The still shells were empty of hope; the moving ones held something already changed. Break a swelling cocoon before it opens and no creature will fly out of that shell. I cannot bring the transformed back. The shallow western gully bends around the grove toward the great roots.

The ribbon was tied around a twig as a marker in a game. Another knot is clenched inside a split shell farther along. The flowers kept growing when the games stopped. This little thing records a person, not a treasure hidden in a creature.

Mikhail, if you reach the camp first: we moved the wounded into the southwestern tent. The creature came out of the northern tent and caught Pavel in the open. Keep behind the canvas and use the gap in the eastern cordon. We are leaving before dusk. — Lena

The last prayer has been crossed out. Beneath it: We barred the front doors to keep the strangers away. Now the footsteps are inside. Irina took the remaining blankets through the sacristy; I could not persuade her to come back for the stone. The western wall is broken. Follow the living while there is still time.

The letters were written on a strip torn from a sleeve: The eastern way is wide enough to carry him, but the scratches there are fresh. I left the iron bar where the prop broke. We came back around the stone chime and reached the brace from below. The peg can be pulled from that side. If he wakes, we will try the ladder before we try the red face again.

A burned clasp is all that remains of the garrison standard. No magic lives in it. Names scratched into the back remember those who held the southern road open. Keep it as testimony; the Carapace Shard belongs to the apostle, not to these fallen soldiers.

Wear the Seal of Severed Flesh to add 20% of each damaging hit against the listed demons, apostles and projections; the extra damage is rounded down after their defenses. Zombies and people receive no extra damage. Closing the Count's exposed breach quiets future incursions near his residence, but does not erase the Brand. Other apostles must be hunted separately.

*Accounts appear here after you read them. The paper itself can be kept as a memory or left behind.

The breaches recorded here are closed. Their surroundings have gained a respite, but the Brand endures and distant wounds remain open. Collect any relics left behind, tend your refuge and keep the surviving records. Beyond these quieted places lies country you have yet to explore.

'The Behelit opened a place of sacrifice along the boundary where our worlds collided. Your Eclipse widened those wounds; it did not create this world's first catastrophe. I could not undo the sacrifice. I cut a way out while someone remained to save.'

The Behelit was a key to a place of sacrifice. The lives offered there were not a toll that bought your safety. You escaped because a way out was cut while you still lived. Do not seek another ceremony as a cure for what it left you.

'The Brand marks a survivor of the sacrifice. Its pain warns you when demons draw near; a stronger presence hurts more. At night, expect them to seek you out. Find cover and leave yourself a way to flee.'

Not every demon follows your Brand. Some have crossed the wounds between worlds and roam on their own; the Brand draws another hunt toward you at night. Quieting its call does not remove creatures already near your bed. A closed wound does not silence the Brand.

A sign of stone and bone quiets the Brand’s new night summons within eight tiles on the same level. It does not stop roaming demons, zombies or attacks. Place your bed within its reach; prepare water, light and an escape route. The sign needs no fuel, but its protection ends when you leave its reach.

Set eight stones and four bones into a protective sign on clear ground. A little wilderness knowledge is enough to arrange it; allow about twenty minutes. Keep your bed within eight steps on the same level. Walls and a clear escape route must do what the sign cannot: shelter you from creatures already here.

Choose a place you can leave as well as defend. Dress your wounds, keep drinking water and bandages near your bed, and leave room to reach the door. Light helps you see what is coming; it is not a ward. Rest before testing your strength against an apostle. A weapon cannot give you back the breath spent running.

Walk the outer ground first. Look for cover, lesser creatures and a way back before entering the keeper’s ground. Watch a heavy attack begin; move aside rather than trade blows through it. A retreat is not a broken oath. Return when your wounds and your equipment allow it, then examine what the fight uncovered.

A keeper holds a particular wound open. When it falls, examine that wound; a victory alone may leave the opening behind. Closing it restrains new crossings nearby. Creatures that have already crossed remain, and distant wounds still feed the dark. Take the evidence with you and read it before choosing another road.

The collision broke more than the ground. Some lives were drawn away from the deaths that awaited them. That does not make every being here a projection. Kill a living original and that life ends; breaking a reflection leaves its source untouched.

'Apostles are monstrous beings with wills and bodies of their own. The God Hand stand apart: they preside over the sacrifice. Void and Griffith are not ordinary apostles. Do not mistake surviving an encounter for defeating them.'
'Some things you met before were projections: an echo formed around a Behelit. Breaking the echo leaves the true being untouched. The Behelit itself was real.'

dynamic_line.yes: A skilled metalworker can make the cannon: fabrication 8, mechanics 4 and the proper tools. Rickert builds that mechanism at Godot's forge if you bring the materials. Either way, fit the finished cannon by activating it in your inventory.
dynamic_line.no: The smiths can help you prepare a blade and mend your equipment.

dynamic_line.yes: Carry the finished prosthetic arm cannon in your inventory and activate it there. The mount where your left hand used to be must still be empty. You need not wield the cannon or find an autodoc to attach it.
dynamic_line.no: The smiths can help you prepare a blade and mend your equipment.

dynamic_line: Keep one road journal for the directions you have learned, the smiths’ orders and the accounts you have read. Read a recovered letter before setting it aside; a sealed page has told you nothing. If a road is uncertain, keep its entry and return to the evidence. When we part, those notes will remain with you.

I follow a war older than your wounds. When I can deny the sacrifice another life, I do. That does not make your road mine to command. Keep the life I carried out of the dark; decide what is worth protecting with it.
Advice you wrote down while speaking with the Skull Knight.

*A broken road, a ruined foundation, ash around a wound in the earth. The vision stayed with you when the voices fell silent. It may lead to another opening between the worlds. The journey is yours to choose; prepare a way to retreat.
